title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) to undergo testing
items.desc: The Texans are having tests done on Nico Collins' hamstring.
items.impact: Collins was limited in practice on Wednesday with the injury. It is unclear if it came up during last week's game or during practice. There should be an update on his status on Thursday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Packers' edge rusher is currently going through the NFL's concussion protocols and was limited on Wednesday as a result. Their defensive front will be weaker than usual if he is unable to suit up and play against the Jets this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Packers' starting right tackle is a new addition to their injury report. He's dealing with a knee injury right now, but it remains unclear whether or not it will threaten his availability for Week 2. Aaron Banks (knee) is also injured right now, so the Packers' offensive line may struggle this week if they are missing multiple of their starters against the Jets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Aaron Banks (knee) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran was unable to play in the team's season opener last week, but he practiced in a limited fashion on Wednesday and seems to have a chance to suit up in Week 2. Green Bay's offense would benefit greatly from the return of one of their starting offensive linemen.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk (finger) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Juszczyk has been dealing with this finger injury for a little while already and was limited at another practice on Wednesday. He was able to play through it last week and will likely do the same in Week 2, which is good news for San Francisco's offense as a whole.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Eddy Pineiro (illness) absent from practice Wednesday
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro (illness) was absent from San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran kicker missed the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday due to an illness that he's currently recovering from. He should be ready to play in time for Week 2, however, and remains a quality fantasy option at the kicker position for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: George Kittle (Achilles) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: George Kittle (Achilles) was limited at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: San Francisco is still being careful with Kittle's workload at this point, so they left him as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday. He should be able to play on Sunday barring any unforeseen setbacks, however, and will likely continue to ramp up his workload over the next few weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dre Greenlaw (rest/Achilles) sidelined at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Dre Greenlaw (rest/Achilles) was sidelined at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: San Francisco gave several veterans the day off on Wednesday, including Greenlaw, who is still nursing an Achilles injury. He should be good to go for Week 2, which is good news for San Francisco's defense heading into a favorable matchup against the Dolphins.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: McCaffrey was a non-participant at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday. The team gave him a routine rest day and he should be back on Thursday, so fantasy managers should have no concerns about him heading into a great Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nick Bosa (rest/knee) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Nick Bosa (rest/knee) missed San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The star edge rusher was held out of Wednesday's practice as part of the planned injury maintenance for his knee. He should be good to go for Week 2 and will remain one of San Francisco's most impactful players moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chop Robinson (concussion) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Chop Robinson (concussion) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran edge rusher is currently in the NFL's concussion protocols and was only able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday as a result. It looks like he will have a good chance to play in Week 2 still, but we won't know until later on in the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) without injury designation for Week 2
items.desc: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) is without an injury designation heading into Week 2.
items.impact: Mitchell was previously battling a hamstring injury, but he was able to play through it in Week 1 and is now off of the injury report entirely heading into Week 2. He should be a full go moving forward but won't have any real fantasy value on this offense for as long as Omarion Hampton remains healthy for the Chargers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jeanty seems to be entirely over his ankle injury at this point, as he played through it in Week 1 and now logs a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. He should be a full go and high-quality fantasy option moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonathan Greenard (pec) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Jonathan Greenard (pec) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran was sidelined due to his pectoral injury in Week 1, but he was able to practice on Wednesday and seems to have a chance to make his return to the lineup in Week 2. Philadelphia's pass rush will get an upgrade whenever he's back in their lineup and fully healthy.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) a non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: DeJean pops up on the injury report to start the week due to a pair of injuries that he is battling. He wasn't able to practice at all on Wednesday, which puts his availability for Week 2 in question. Philadelphia has multiple key defenders on the injury report right now, so their defense could be weaker than usual in a matchup against the Titans this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Carter (wrist) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Jalen Carter (wrist) did not take part in Philadelphia's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The star defensive tackle wasn't able to take part in practice on Wednesday. He's dealing with a wrist injury right now, and it's possible that it will threaten his availability for Week 2. Philadelphia's defensive front will be weaker than usual if he is ruled out for this matchup against the Titans.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dalton Schultz (rest) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Dalton Schultz (rest) missed Houston's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran tight end was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day to start the week. He is likely to be back at practice on Thursday and should play in Week 2, barring anything unforeseen between now and then. He remains a fringe streaming option at the tight end position at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joe Burrow (back) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Joe Burrow (back) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Burrow was listed as a limited participant on the team's first official injury report of the week on Wednesday. He's dealing with some back soreness right now and wasn't able to throw passes at practice as a result. He told reporters that he plans on playing in Week 2, but this is worth monitoring over the next few days, as Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown will all have their projections affected if Burrow is sidelined or playing at less than 100% health against a tough Texans' defense this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Fautanu (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Troy Fautanu (ankle) missed Pittsburgh's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Steelers could be without their starting left tackle this week, as Fautanu missed Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury that he sustained at some point. His absence would be bad news for Pittsburgh's offense ahead of a tough matchup against the Patriots this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning) logs limited practice Wednesday
items.desc: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning) logged a limited practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: It looks like Porter is nearing a return to the field for Pittsburgh, as he was able to log a limited practice session on Wednesday. He is also no longer listed with a back injury but is only limited while he ramps up his conditioning. His return, whenever it comes, will provide a significant boost to the Steelers' secondary moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Pittman is a new addition to Pittsburgh's injury report, being listed with a foot issue that left him limited at the team's first practice of the week. In the off-chance that it affects his availability or workload for Week 2, fantasy managers should expect more work for Pat Freiermuth against the Patriots.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Washington (personal) absent from practice Wednesday
items.desc: Darnell Washington (personal) was absent from Pittsburgh's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Washington was not able to practice for the Steelers on Wednesday as he tends to a personal issue of some kind. It seems unlikely that it will affect his availability for Sunday's game against the Patriots, but either way he remains of off the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cole Van Lanen (knee) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Cole Van Lanen (knee) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Van Lanen was able to play through his knee injury in Week 1, but he's still dealing with it and was limited at practice on Wednesday as a result. He should be available to play in Week 2, however, barring any unforeseen setbacks with his recovery between now and then.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at Jacksonville's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury in Week 1 which left him limited at practice on Wednesday. It doesn't seem to be a serious issue for the young wideout, but it still could affect his workload in Week 2's matchup against the Broncos. Fantasy managers should continue to pay attention to updates about his status moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was able to play through his thumb injury last week, but he's not fully over it and it left him limited at practice on Wednesday. He should play through it again this week but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy asset for the foreseeable future, unless Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) misses time for Jacksonville.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) considered limited Wednesday
items.desc: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) was considered a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran linebacker was dealing with a wrist injury on Wednesday and was unable to practice in a full capacity for the Jaguars. It's likely that he will play in Week 2 still, but we won't know for sure until later on in the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) a limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Allen was technically active for Sunday's game against the Browns, but he didn't see a single touch in the team's blowout win. That could have something to do with his hip injury, which left him limited at practice again on Wednesday. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: A chest injury left the veteran linebacker limited at the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It could threaten his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Bears, which is less than ideal with Blake Cashman (wrist) also uncertain to play in that game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Blake Cashman (wrist) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Blake Cashman (wrist) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Minnesota's defensive front could be weaker than usual this week, with both Cashman and Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) limited at practice due to injury. The absence of one or both of them would be less than ideal in a tough matchup against Chicago's offense this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Jauan Jennings (personal) did not take part in Minnesota's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was absent from Minnesota's practice on Wednesday due to a personal issue of some kind. It seems unlikely to affect his availability for Week 2, but he remains squarely off of the fantasy radar after going catchless in the season opener last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian O'Neill (knee) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Brian O'Neill (knee) was limited at Minnesota's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Minnesota's starting right tackle is at risk of missing this week's game, with O'Neill being limited at practice on Wednesday due to a knee issue. His absence would be less than ideal for whichever quarterback is at the helm for the Vikings this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyler Murray (concussion) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Kyler Murray (concussion) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Murray comes through as a limited participant on Minnesota's official injury report on Wednesday. He's on track to be cleared in time for Week 2 and will likely have a chance to play, although that is far from certain at this point. Carson Wentz will likely serve as the starter once again if Murray is sidelined against the Bears, which would be great news for Justin Jefferson.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Audric Estime (thigh) placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Audric Estime (thigh) was recently placed on injured reserve, knocking him out for at least four weeks.
items.impact: Estime lands on injured reserve due to a thigh injury. He will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks, but he wasn't a big part of New Orleans' backfield rotation either way, so his absence won't have much of an impact from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Alvin Kamara (knee) logged a full practice session on Wednesday and seems likely to play in Week 2 against the Baltimore Ravens.
items.impact: The veteran running back logged a full practice session on Wednesday. He seems likely to play in Week 2, with Head coach Kellen Moore telling reporters that he feels good about Kamara's chances of suiting up. His likely return this week would mean less work for Kendre Miller moving forward and could mean a slight decrease in work for Travis Etienne Jr. as well.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Juwan Johnson (illness) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Juwan Johnson (illness) did not take part in New Orleans' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Johnson is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report, being listed with an illness of some kind that left him absent from practice on Wednesday. He's likely considered day-to-day at this point and seems to have a good chance to play in Week 2. If he's active he will be worth starting in a big matchup against the Ravens on Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cameron Jordan (hamstring) upgraded to limited Wednesday
items.desc: Cameron Jordan (hamstring) was upgraded to a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran was able to make his return to practice on Wednesday. He has missed some time while recovering from a hamstring injury, but it looks like he may be back in the lineup as soon as Week 2. New Orleans' defensive front will be stronger and have more depth when he's available to suit up for them again.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Devontez Walker (groin) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: Devontez Walker (groin) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: Walker logged a full practice session on Wednesday despite missing last week's game due to a groin injury of some kind. It looks like he will be back in the lineup in Week 2, which is great timing given that the Ravens will be without Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) and possibly Zay Flowers (hamstring) in their matchup against the Saints this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Teddye Buchanan (knee) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Teddye Buchanan (knee) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Buchanan may be available to make his return to the lineup in Week 2 after missing the season opener last week. He was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday, and it would be a big boost for the Ravens if they were able to get one of their starting linebackers back in the lineup this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: John Simpson (groin) absent from practice Wednesday
items.desc: John Simpson (groin) was absent from Baltimore's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Ravens may be without their starting left guard on Sunday, who missed their first practice of the week on Wednesday due to a groin injury. LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) was also a non-participant, so Baltimore's offensive line could be much weaker than usual on one side if one or both of those guys are sidelined this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited at Baltimore's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Madubuike missed the team's season opener last week due to a neck issue, but it looks like his health is improving, as he was able to take part in Wednesday's practice in a limited fashion. His return this week would provide a significant boost for Baltimore's defensive front, which would be very timely with a tough matchup against the Saints coming up.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ronnie Stanley (toe) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Ronnie Stanley (toe) did not take part in practice for the Ravens on Wednesday.
items.impact: A toe injury left Stanley sidelined at practice on Wednesday. It's still early in the week, so it's possible this is nothing more than injury management for the veteran. His status is worth monitoring throughout the week, especially with LG John Simpson (groin) also missing practice.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) a non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Trey Hendrickson (finger) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The star edge rusher was not able to partake in Wednesday's practice due to a finger injury that he's managing. It remains to be seen if it will threaten his availability for Week 2, but that would be tough for the Ravens ahead of a challenging matchup against New Orleans' offense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) officially misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Zay Flowers (hamstring) officially missed Baltimore's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Flowers was not able to participate in Baltimore's first practice of the week on Wednesday. He's dealing with a hamstring injury that he aggravated in Week 1, and it's currently unclear whether or not he will suit up for Week 2's matchup against the Saints. If he's sidelined, fantasy managers should expect Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews to both see more work with rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) also out of the lineup now.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyson Bagent (back) without injury designation for Week 2
items.desc: Tyson Bagent (back) is without an injury designation ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Bagent missed Chicago's season opener on Sunday due to a back issue, but he seems to be fully healthy at this point and carries no injury designation ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Vikings. He will likely reclaim the QB2 spot from Case Keenum, who was the backup in his absence last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rome Odunze (calf) off injury report for Week 2
items.desc: Rome Odunze (calf) carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Odunze has been recovering from a calf injury for a while, but it seems that he is fully over it at this point, as he isn't listed on Chicago's injury report at all heading into Week 2. It's likely that his workload will ramp up this week after he was limited in the season opener, which should help him to produce a fantasy finish better than his underwhelming performance in Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Odafe Oweh (calf) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Odafe Oweh (calf) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Oweh was a limited participant on Wednesday due to a calf injury, but he was able to play through that issue last week, so it looks likely that he will do so again in Week 2. His presence is crucial for Washington's defensive front, which already lacks depth to begin with.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daron Payne (knee) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Daron Payne (knee) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran was able to play through his knee injury in Week 1 but reverted back to being limited at practice on Wednesday. This is likely a load management tactic for the Commanders, so it looks likely that he will be available to face up against the Cowboys this week, which is great news for Washington's defense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) limited Wednesday
items.desc: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) was limited for the Commanders on Wednesday.
items.impact: Chaisson wasn't able to log a full practice session on Wednesday due to his knee injury, but he played through it last week, so it doesn't seem like a serious threat to his availability for Week 2. The Commanders will need him in what projects to be a tough matchup against the Cowboys this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: Surprisingly, the rookie was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday after suffering a shoulder injury in Monday's win over the Broncos. It looks like he will be able to play in Week 2, which is great news for the Chiefs ahead of a matchup against the Colts.
